transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I suppose I'm here because... I keep hearing Garrett's voice. 

It's... it's as clear as if he's standing right behind me on the trail. Or in my painting room. And... I mean, logically, part of me knows he's dead. But in the moment... it just feels completely real.
Is it always Garrett's voice that you hear?
Yeah. Just... just his. Like I said, it's... it's just Garrett. Nobody else.
Does Garrett's voice tell you to do things or is it more like a conversation?

No... he doesn't tell me to do things. It's not like that. 

It's just... like I was saying, it feels like he's standing right there behind me. Just talking to me. Like normal. Even though the rational part of my brain knows he's gone, when it happens... it's just completely real to me. I don't really want to get into the specifics of what we talk about.
How long have you been hearing Garrett's voice?
Um... well, it started after he passed. So... about a month now. It's just been this whole... crisis, I guess, for the last month.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time since Garrett passed away?

I don't... I wouldn't really say that. I don't know if sad is the right word. I haven't really been focusing on... on how I feel, I guess. I just haven't thought about it like that. It's just been a lot to deal with.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy since Garrett passed away?

I guess so. Yeah. I mean... I haven't really been doing much of anything. 

Usually, I paint, or play guitar... I do some theater stuff. And my work with patients, obviously. But... I don't know. Lately, it just feels... flat. Like I'm just going through the motions. None of it really means anything right now. It just feels out of reach.
Do you have difficulty falling asleep or sleeping too much since Garrett passed away?

Um... sleep has been... difficult. For a few weeks, I was only getting maybe two or three hours a night... but I felt completely wired. Now, it's just... I crash. It's this heavy, broken sleep, but I still wake up before the sun, just... exhausted. And panicked, I guess. It's not good.
Do you feel guilty about anything related to Garrett's death?

I... yeah, I guess. It's... I just keep replaying things in my head. Every last conversation I had with Garrett. And... even work. Every patient session I've cancelled. 

I just... I've convinced myself I failed everyone. Sometimes it just feels like... like people would be better off if I weren't in the way.
Have you been having any unusual thoughts or beliefs since Garrett passed away?
Um... no. I don't think so. I'm not really sure what you mean by unusual, but... no. Just what I already told you.
Have you been feeling like you're worthless or that you don't deserve to be happy since Garrett passed away?

I... yeah. That's... kind of what I just meant. When I said I've convinced myself I failed everyone. You don't really feel like you deserve much when you're just... letting everyone down. Like I said, it just seems like they'd all be better off without me in the way.
Have you seen things that other people can't see since Garrett passed away?

I haven't... seen anything. But... I hear him. Garrett, I mean. It's... it's why I came in. I hear his voice. It's not just a memory, it's... it's like he's right there. Standing behind me when I'm out on the trail, or... or when I'm in my painting room. It's so clear. I know he's gone, I know that, but... when it happens, it just feels so real.
Have you been thinking about death or wanting to die since Garrett passed away?

I... yeah. Sometimes. I just... I think about not waking up. It happens a lot. And... there was a day recently where it just felt... too close. I had to tell my wife I didn't think I should be left alone. I just... I didn't trust myself.
Have your conversations with Garrett's voice interfered with your daily activities?

I... yes. It did. I had to stop seeing my own patients. I was cancelling sessions, couldn't keep up with my notes. It just... wasn't safe for me to practice. And at home... like I said, my wife had to call the crisis team because I couldn't be by myself. Coming to the hospital... it was just the point where everything stopped. Work, home... everything.
How often do you hear Garrett's voice?
I... I don't really know. I haven't kept track of it. It's just... hard to say exactly. Sometimes.
Have you ever thought that your thoughts are being controlled by someone or something else?
I... no. I don't think so. My thoughts are my own.
Do you think Garrett's voice is real or just a product of your mind?

I... part of me knows he's dead. I do know that. But... when it happens, it feels completely real. It's as clear as if he's standing right behind me... like when I'm out on the trail, or in my painting room. In the moment, it just... it's real to me.
Do you feel like you've lost pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy most of the time since Garrett passed away?

I guess so, yeah. Everything just feels... flat. The things that usually anchor me... painting, playing guitar... even rehearsing at the theater or just sitting with my own patients. It's all... unreachable. Like I'm just going through the motions of a life that stopped meaning anything.
Do you think your hearing Garrett's voice is the main thing that's been bothering you, or is it more the feelings of emptiness and not enjoying things?
I don't know... it's hard to separate them. The voice is... jarring. But the emptiness is just... always there. I guess they both bother me. I'm not sure which is worse.
How long have you been feeling this emptiness?
I'd say... about four months. That's how long this... shut-down part has been going on.
Have you been experiencing intense yearning or longing for Garrett for the past month?
I don't really know. I wouldn't call it that. It's not... yearning, exactly. Just... what I said before. The emptiness.
